[Management API](admin-api.html)

The Grant Negotiation and Authorization Protocol (RFC 9635) and its resource server connections (RFC 9767): the authorization server of this realm, what the applications using it have done, and the two things an operator does to its state by hand.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## GET /admin-api/gnap

`getGnap`

**The GNAP authorization server: endpoints, capabilities, grants, resource sets, settings**

Everything /admin/gnap draws. The endpoints of this realm's GNAP authorization server (RFC 9635) and its RS-facing API (RFC 9767); the section 9 capabilities of the default authorization server and of each named one (paged, `serversPage`, answered by `authorizationServersPaging`), after that profile's GNAP overrides — which are what each grant endpoint ENFORCES; the five token formats and the public material that verifies the self-contained ones; the grants this realm holds (paged, `grantsPage`, and filtered by `state`); the registered resource sets (paged, `resourcesPage`); and the `gnap.*` settings, which are written through POST /admin-api/config/set-many.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/gnap` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The authorization server as the page draws it.

## POST /admin-api/gnap/delete-resource-set

`deleteGnapResourceSet`

**Delete a registered resource set (RFC 9767 section 3.4)**

Removes the resource set, after which its reference no longer resolves in a grant request. Tokens already issued keep the rights they carry.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/gnap` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reference` | string | yes | The resource reference, from GET /admin-api/gnap. |

**200**: The reference that was deleted.

| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `reference` | string |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/gnap/monitor

`getGnapMonitor`

**Every application that uses GNAP, and what each has done**

Everything /admin/gnap/monitor draws: one row per application declared for GNAP, seen speaking it, or counted — client instances and resource servers — with the grants it holds by state, its live tokens, and its counters since the process started: grants requested, approved and denied, tokens issued by format, rotations, revocations, failed key proofs, introspections, registrations, derivations, and the GNAP error codes it was answered with. Per trust realm, and with no reset: the durable record is GET /admin-api/audit.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/gnap/monitor` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The totals, and one row per application.

## POST /admin-api/gnap/revoke-grant

`revokeGnapGrant`

**Revoke a GNAP grant, as its client could (RFC 9635 section 5.4)**

Finalizes the grant and revokes every access token issued under it, through the same path the client's own DELETE on the continuation URI takes — so the client sees exactly what it would have seen had it revoked the grant itself, and a CAEP session-revoked is sent to every stream that takes it. A grant already finalized is reported unchanged rather than refused — except one finalized as `issued`, whose tokens are still live and are revoked (#432). Naming `user` as well revokes it only if that person is its resource owner — the per-person door the GNAP grants tab of /admin/users uses, whose grants GET /admin-api/users?user= lists as `gnapGrants`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/gnap` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grant` | string | yes | The grant identifier, from GET /admin-api/gnap or the person's `gnapGrants`. |
| `user` | string |  | The person whose grant it must be (optional). A grant whose resource owner is somebody else is refused and nothing changes. |

**200**: The grant as it now stands.
